body.statement: Construct one total test that, using the lexicographically first minimizer in \(\mathcal K_n\), has rejection probability at most \(a_0\) uniformly on \(\mathcal H_0\) for every \(n\), type-II error at most \(b_0\) whenever \(D(P)\ge C r_{\mathrm{test}}(n)\), deterministic tuning, and stated arithmetic and memory costs through dense and sparse occupancy regimes. A valid target cost is \(O(|\mathcal K_n|n+\sum_{\mathbf k\in\mathcal K_n}R(\mathbf k))\) arithmetic and \(O(\max_{\mathbf k\in\mathcal K_n}R(\mathbf k))\) memory, with any sharper certified implementation recorded. Next prove \(r_{\mathrm{mix}}(n)\asymp r_{\mathrm{test}}(n)\) with constants depending only on \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,d,L\). Only after that equivalence is established, denote their common order by \(r_{\mathrm{sharp}}(n;\alpha,\beta,\gamma,d,L)\), simplify it in every regime including equality-case logarithms, and conclude \(\rho_n^*\asymp r_{\mathrm{sharp}}\). If the two deterministic optimizations do not match, state the remaining upper--lower gap instead of defining a common rate.
body.justification: This remains the field-tier theorem target: it requires a total uniformly calibrated test and an original fixed-\(n\), constant-null-supported converse on the identical class, followed by an independent optimization match.
body.gap: The prescribed four-atom law satisfies the requested marginal moments, class-side inequalities, one-observation matching, and cross-fine singleton-pair cancellation.  The first surviving mixed-occupancy term is now explicit: a same-fine pair plus a distinct-fine singleton has third canonical projection \(\delta^2\mathcal L_{12}\kappa_3\), contributing \((n)_3h^dH^d\delta^4\) on the squared likelihood scale.  It diverges at the proposed rough stress rate, so this lower construction does not support the desired converse.  A replacement cancellation or comparison, the matching upper concentration theorem, and the all-regime optimization are still missing.
body.consumer: A completed theorem would give causal-forest calibration and epidemiologic heterogeneity workflows a genuine detectability benchmark and an omnibus finite-sample procedure, without certifying any fitted forest or converting non-rejection into a homogeneity conclusion.

obligation.what_is_open: Construct a different bounded constant-null-supported nested prior whose exact fixed-sample likelihood cancels the nonzero cross-fine third canonical projection in \(\texttt{lem:four-atom-cross-fine-third-projection}\), or derive an alternative comparison that controls it at the desired scale; then prove the matching sparse-occupancy upper theorem and optimize the independent lower and upper maps in every regime.
obligation.obstruction: For the prescribed four-atom law, conditional one-observation matching and independence do cancel two observations in distinct fine cells, and the same-fine residual is subdominant at the stress scale.  But a same-fine pair multiplied by the common singleton factor in a distinct fine cell leaves the exact third canonical coefficient \(\delta^2\mathcal L_{12}\kappa_3\).  Its squared likelihood contribution is at least of order \((n)_3h^dH^d\delta^4\), which equals \(n^{1/3}\) at \(d=\gamma=1\), \(\alpha=\beta=1/10\), \(h=\delta^5\), \(H=\delta\), and \(\delta=n^{-4/15}\).  Thus the required support-controlled lower envelope does not close for this exact law, so no independent optimization match or definition of \(r_{\mathrm{sharp}}\) is justified.
obligation.attempted: The calculation verified the four atomic probabilities, all first and second coordinate moments, the construction-side margin and Hölder inequalities, exact one-observation matching, and exact two-singleton cross-fine cancellation.  It then expanded the shared-fine two-observation factors without a remainder, multiplied by the distinct-fine singleton factor, averaged the macro sign, subtracted all lower-coordinate marginals, and computed the resulting third canonical projection and its spatial \(L^2\) scale.  The mandated stress substitution shows this term diverges while the same-fine term vanishes and the proposed fourth-order term stays bounded.
obligation.partial_result:
The already established unchanged-class bracket remains
\[
 c n^{-2\gamma/(4\gamma+d)}\leq\rho_n^*\leq Cb_n,\qquad
 b_n=\begin{cases}
 n^{-2t/(4t+d)},&d\leq4t,\\
 n^{-4t/(4t+3d)},&d>4t,
 \end{cases}\qquad t=\min\{\gamma,\alpha+\beta\},                    \tag{1}
\]
for all sufficiently large \(n\).  If \(\alpha+\beta\geq\gamma\) and \(d\leq4\gamma\), then
\[
 \rho_n^*\asymp\rho_{n,e}^*\asymp n^{-2\gamma/(4\gamma+d)},          \tag{2}
\]
and \(d=4\gamma\) carries no logarithm in this proved subregion.

For the newly prescribed bounded four-atom law, all coordinate means vanish, the squares are fixed, and
\[
 {\mathbb E}_0(U_jV_j\mid\sigma_Q)-{\mathbb E}_1(U_jV_j)
 =\delta\sigma_Q.
\]
The original binary margins and all three Hölder conditions follow from the explicit amplitude inequalities in \(\texttt{lem:four-atom-cross-fine-third-projection}\).  Conditional one-observation matching is exact, and independence across distinct fine-coordinate pairs cancels the two-singleton cross-fine term exactly.  Nevertheless, for observations \(1,2\) in one fine cell and observation \(3\) in a distinct fine cell in the same macro cube, the third canonical likelihood projection equals
\[
 \delta^2\mathcal L_{12}\kappa_3,\qquad
 \mathcal L_{12}
 =(\xi_1+\xi_2)(\upsilon_1+\upsilon_2)
 -(1+q_e^2\xi_1\xi_2)(\kappa_1+\kappa_2),                            \tag{3}
\]
and is not identically zero.  Its squared \(L^2(P_\star^{\otimes n})\) contribution is at least a fixed multiple of
\[
 (n)_3h^dH^d\delta^4.                                                \tag{4}
\]
At \(d=\gamma=1\), \(\alpha=\beta=1/10\), \(h=\delta^5\), \(H=\delta\), and \(\delta=n^{-4/15}\), the same-fine term is \(n^{-2/5}\), the proposed fourth-order term is one, but (4) is \(n^{1/3}\).  Thus the exact four-atom lower construction does not deliver the proposed candidate frontier.  A different bounded prior that cancels (3), or an alternative fixed-sample comparison controlling it at the desired scale, is required before the matching upper statistic and all-regime optimization can settle the target.  The two frozen optimizations remain diagnostics, and \(r_{\mathrm{sharp}}\) remains undefined.
